summary: The proposal preserves the Tasks/Review transaction boundary, separate Identity/CRT authority, durable command/feed recovery, and a stopped-writer PostgreSQL cutover. The Smart Add binding, authenticated cross-process SSE, resource-ownership responses, native suggestion entry points, dependent-action resolution, and AI cancellation contracts are now specified. One remaining consequential contract disagreement concerns legacy consent revocation using an already-used idempotency key. This was a read-only planning review; no build, product test, migration, sizing measurement, or human acceptance was performed.

findings.description: The universal legacy owner/key-to-one-receipt mapping does not preserve the accepted consent-revocation collision exception. A supported legacy caller can grant consent with key K and then revoke using K: the existing contract requires a successful 204, retains the grant receipt, and records a separate replay-safe revoke effect. PR-28 moves that revoke into a boundary whose current specification maps K to the original single receipt and refuses changed operation/content. Following that mapping would reject the revoke as IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED and leave cloud consent active, violating preserved legacy behavior and FR-014/019. The catalog promises owner-wide revocation but does not define how this existing replay exception survives the conflicting general mapping.
evidence: specs/026-rust-core-sync/contracts/sync-v1.md:57 maps each legacy (owner_id, idempotency_key) to one durable receipt and forbids an operation-dependent replay namespace; :60 returns IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED without execution for different normalized content.

specs/026-rust-core-sync/contracts/command-catalog.md:46 requires one legacy receipt identity across transports with original-operation reuse checks; :35 says consent revocation preserves current owner-wide semantics.
specs/026-rust-core-sync/tasks.md:87 (T028/PR-28) routes Navigator consent grant and revoke through this command boundary.

specs/020-weekly-review/contracts/http.md:696-708 explicitly requires revoke using another command's key to succeed, keep the original receipt, and record its own replay so a later retry cannot revoke a newer grant.
backend/app/modules/tasks/navigator.py:889-940, NavigatorService.revoke_consent, implements this exception using _revoke_collision_key while preserving the original owner/key record.

backend/tests/test_review_navigator.py:1271, test_020_FR_024_a_grant_key_reused_by_a_revoke_still_revokes, requires 204 and consent_current false; :1291, test_020_FR_024_a_colliding_revoke_retry_never_revokes_a_newer_grant, preserves the later grant on retry.
findings.recommendation: Specify a narrow legacy consent-revoke translation exception before ordinary changed-operation conflict handling: retain the existing owner/key receipt, derive one durable revoke-effect identity consistently across legacy transports, and replay that revoke effect without changing a newer grant. Publish its consent change through the same atomic receipt/feed transaction. Keep strict changed-content rejection for ordinary legacy commands and device-originated command IDs; reuse the existing collision/retry tests when implementing PR-28.
